### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_
- `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface NonHostDeclaringPackage))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `11d1ef7a45fcc701d91c06f2558b565b7d0bd6cc` — the merge of head `5c706cd33a2aa2abbd4a7ac7a5ac54c8d675f31f` into base `da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 11d1ef7a45fcc701d91c06f2558b565b7d0bd6cc && git checkout 11d1ef7a45fcc701d91c06f2558b565b7d0bd6cc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72 5c706cd33a2aa2abbd4a7ac7a5ac54c8d675f31f && git checkout -B drift-repro da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72 && git merge --no-ff 5c706cd33a2aa2abbd4a7ac7a5ac54c8d675f31f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-materialization.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-overlay-reads.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/stored-connector-package-ref.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/28594-stored-connector-file-ref.md, .changeset/28594-stored-row-package-binding.md + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`getArtifactItem`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`_registry`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (the `objectql` service, Phase-2 hydration, `metadata:reloaded` triggers), packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts (the reload trigger), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`getMetaItemsForExecution`, `stripDerivedProvenance`, `stateTenantAuthorship`, `withRowBinding`, `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry`, `isSealedManagedItem`, the by-name and draft stamp sites), packages/metadata-core/src/code-artifact-provenance.ts (`isTenantAuthored`), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (its reload triggers), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs and scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (the level axis), content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx (read for the narrowing's prose, not reviewed here)

Read at 2026-11-01T13:04Z, read-only: the diff `f23e0512..43953ed3` (merge-base with `origin/main`, 8 files, 3 commits), card #28594 (body, triage 6555201152, claim 6557460226, os-dev-report 6558199261 as claims to verify), the seat's order and private hand-back, PR #28671's body and check-runs, card #28534 and PR #28587 (`d2c487407`) with its review 6554878186, open PR #28651's file list and its `connectors.mdx` hunk. Nothing built or run. Check-runs on the head at read time: 15 success, 11 skipped, 21 still in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1–8, the Type Check and Lint families, Build Docs, Live E2E UI), **1 failure: `Check Changeset`** (both PR Automation runs on this head; see ②). This is a host-file exposure class: this record states judgments in product words and carries no reproduction, path or mechanism.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Premise.** The card's reach was read from code; the dev measured it through the real metadata door on base and it holds: a stored environment-wide row, an `authored` package's row, a stored stdio transport and a stored row whose body named the host's package all materialized as the host's. Consistent with the base code I read (`nonHostDeclaringPackageOf` at base answered "host" for any unstamped entry and for any `code` stamp).
- **One classifier (item 1).** Yes. `nonHostDeclaringPackageOf` is extended with one more answer (`why: 'stored'`) and `createInstalledPackageRefRefusal` is the one refusal, with a third wording branch for a stored entry (entry, its package if any, the ref, the remedy). No second predicate, no second message function; the message interpolates only the entry name, the package id and the author's own ref, pinned by `not.toContain(path.resolve(fixtureRoot))` in two unit cases. The remedy text differs from an installed entry's (inline or http(s) URL rather than `os build`), which is the same rule said for the right audience, not a second spelling.
- **Who reads the host root (item 2).** At head an entry reads the host root only when (a) its stamp names a `code` row or a `code` residual AND a package registration filed a connector of that name under that package with the same `provider` + `providerConfig` (`SchemaRegistry.getArtifactItem('connector', name, packageId)`, which excludes any tenant-authored body because hydration marks every stored row `_provenance: 'org'` before registering it, #16702), or (b) the entry object itself is one the host's own artifact reload carried (`metadata:reloaded` with `metadata.connectors`). I verified the only production trigger that passes `metadata.connectors` is the metadata plugin's dev reload of the on-disk artifact (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts:1537`); the objectql, runtime-packages and install-local triggers pass `{ changed }` only, so no stored row can arrive as a "carried" host entry. A body stamp is never trusted on its own: a `code` stamp without a filed binding is `stored`, and an `authored` row or no stamp is `stored`. Registry-stamped, never body-stamped: holds.
- **Stored, authored, environment and stdio rows (item 3).** All four refused, by both suites: unit cases for an environment-wide row, an `authored` package's row, a row claiming the host's package, a row under the host's registered name with another binding, and `resolvePackagePath('.')` (the stdio form); the dogfood pins the same four through the real door on one boot, each absent from the listing with a reconcile record naming the entry, its ref and the remedy. A stored stdio transport is refused through `resolvePackagePath`, the one member the MCP factory dereferences; no third road into the root was added.
- **Inline and URL controls (item 4).** Unchanged. A stored inline document and a stored http(s) URL list `ready` with their operation in the dogfood (base and head); the unit control shows neither member is reached for an inline entry. The host's own file-ref and stdio entries keep listing `ready` with their own actions in the same boot, and the unit control pins the host's `code` package and `code` residual reading under the root, judged by binding rather than identity.
- **Column wins (item 5).** `storedOverlayEntries` now serves a row's `_packageId` from its column only, on a copy: replaced when bound to another package, dropped when bound to none. Four unit cases pin it, including the no-write-through guarantee. It feeds both `getMetaItems` and `getMetaItemsForExecution` (the read the materializer uses post-boot). Judgment in ④.
- **Fail-open for doubles (item 6).** `registeredDeclaration` is `undefined` only when the registry object has no `getArtifactItem`; then an unstamped or `code`-stamped entry keeps the base reading. In production the `objectql` service is registered once (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:832`) with `ObjectQL`, whose registry is always a `SchemaRegistry` (`engine.ts:5113`), which has `getArtifactItem`. No `objectql` service at all already meant "host" at base (no door could have registered a package), and the protocol service cannot exist without it. No production path lacks the registered layer; the fail-open is reachable only from test doubles.
- **Tests and ablation.** The dev's three ablations map one-to-one onto the three mechanisms (origin check, column wins, carried-entry reading) and each reds exactly the cases it should; I read the assertions, not the runs. The dogfood's self-stamp case writes the row at rest with a system update because the save door strips the stamp — the correct way to pin a row "another writer stored".
- **Docs row.** The failure-modes row names the doors, the remedy and the rule; it carries no path and no walk-through. Accurate to the mechanism as built.
- **Overlap (item 9).** PR #28651 (`0537d24f`, draft) touches `service-automation/src/connector-credentials-ui.ts` and a different region of `connectors.mdx` (the OAuth connections prose at ~:640, this PR's row is at ~:869). No shared hunk; whichever lands second merges cleanly on today's trees. No other open PR touches `plugin.ts` or `protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts`.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct. The stored shape and the save door are unchanged; what narrows is which package a row is served under, a driver-posture narrowing, which ruling A grades `patch`.
- `@objectstack/service-automation` `patch` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: **inconsistent, and `Check Changeset` is red on it.** The level axis (ruling A, 2026-10-21, on #25105; `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) reads the kind once for the PR: `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on one package the diff moves, and this PR grades every moved package `patch`. PR #28587 carried the same `narrowed` line on its `service-automation` changeset and passed only because its `objectql` and `cloud-connection` changesets were `minor`. The kind is honest here (a value an author writes in a stored connector, a package-relative ref, is now refused: the axis's own definition of `narrowed`), so the grade is what is wrong. Must-fix M1 below.
- Both declaration lines read as declared through the one reader (`clause2-line.mjs`: value `no`, arm `narrowing`; kind `narrowed` / `none`), the parenthetical after `narrowed` is tolerated decoration. `packages/spec/authorable-surface` did not move, so the `added`-and-`spec`-minor rule does not apply. Both changesets carry a BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 `no-migration-prescription` disposition; `check-adr-0087-registration` is not among the red checks.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm for both: a connector that was `ready` is now refused, and a row's served package can only shrink to its column's; the only new "reads" answer (the carried reload payload) already read the root at base. Nothing widened.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Boundary change: what a definition stored in the environment may read or launch on the host. Intended: nothing (only the host's own stack reads its root). As built: the same, keyed on two inputs the stored row cannot write — the registry's filed declaration and the identity of the reload payload — so a row cannot opt out through its body. The M1 class of PR #28587 (a self-written stamp) is closed at the list read (column wins) and, independently, at the classifier (a stamp without a filed binding is `stored`).
- Boot posture: the hand-back's restart control covers installed packages, not a refused stored row already at rest. Should-fix S1 (detail sent to the dev privately).
- The hand-back's edge 5 (the artifact lookup's bare-key fallback answering a hydrated overlay): I confirm it needs a stored row of a shipped connector name, and shipped connectors are sealed (`isSealedManagedItem`: artifact-backed, and `connector` opens no overlay channel), so the save door refuses that row; and the hydrated row would be tenant-authored, which the lookup excludes. Closed on two counts; noted, not flagged.
- Out-of-scope note (item 7): see ④.
- No `packages/spec` change; the claim's file surface is respected; `protocol.ts` is not touched. Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (the card thread's relay), no second author to name.
- The PR body's Acceptance-notes line says `check:skill-examples` is NOT MEASURED; the hand-back says it was re-run and passed, and only `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is unmeasured. A body line to correct when the seat edits the body for M1 (prose, not a verdict matter).

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing holds against the contract it makes real: `ConnectorProviderContext.loadPackageFile` / `resolvePackagePath` resolve "against the root of the package that declared the entry", and a stored definition declares nothing and has no root, so refusing it is the spec's own sentence enforced, not a capability taken away. Per `hits` file:

- `plugin.ts`: the classifier's new branch asks the one question that matters (did a registering door file this binding under this package) and reads it from the registry's artifact layer, which the stored-row hydrator cannot pollute. The binding comparison (`provider` + `providerConfig`, stable-stringified) is the right key: it is everything a factory dereferences a ref out of, so a row served over a registered name with another binding is refused while an equal binding names only refs the host itself declared. The carried-entry road is scoped to object identity of the one trustworthy payload. Holds.
- `protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts` (**item 5, the order's M1-parity ruling**): the order asked for M1's form. M1 refuses at a registration door, where an author is present and the item is not yet filed; `storedOverlayEntries` is a list read, where refusing one row fails every list of the type for every caller or hides the row from the Studio that could fix it. "Column wins" is the save door's existing rule (`stripDerivedProvenance`: the server states provenance, a caller never does) applied at the read, and it is the stronger answer for this site: no caller can be told a package the column does not record. I judge it correct and sufficient on a list read. It leaves no self-stamp road to the materializer: the materializer reads this list post-boot (stamps are the column's), reads the registry pre-boot (a hydrated row is marked tenant-authored, so it can never satisfy the filed-binding check whatever stamp it wears), and the classifier refuses a `code` stamp without a filed binding in any case. The dev's claim that the security fix does not depend on this choice is right; the choice is still the honest read. Accepted as a reasoned deviation, not a must-fix.
- `connector-materialization.test.ts`, `protocol-stored-overlay-reads.test.ts`, the dogfood: each pins what the PR claims, the controls are the right ones (inline, URL, the host's file-ref and stdio entries, the carried reload), and the dogfood measures through the real door.
- **Item 7, the by-name and draft stamp sites in `protocol.ts` (hand-back 3).** Exposure or read-honesty? I traced each: the by-name active read and draft preview serve one item to a caller; the draft list serves drafts, which the execution read does not merge; the view-expansion site is views; `withRowBinding` runs at hydration, where `stateTenantAuthorship` follows it and marks the row tenant-authored, so the registered item can never pass as an artifact (`getArtifactItem` excludes it, the save-door overlay gate and the lock envelope read artifacts only). None of them feeds the materializer's post-boot read, and the one that feeds its pre-boot read (hydration) is defeated by the filed-binding check. No authorization or package-binding decision I found keys on the served body's stamp. **Read-honesty gap only** (a by-name or draft read can still echo a stamp the save door would strip), class b as the dev filed it. **Recommendation: dispatch a follow-up**, not fold in: it is five sites in `protocol.ts` outside the claim's surface, best closed by one shared "the column's binding" helper that `withRowBinding` can become, with its own by-name and draft cases; nothing in this PR's security claim waits on it.
- `.changeset` pair: the metadata-protocol entry is right; the service-automation entry's grade contradicts its own kind (②).

Must-fix and should-fix, one line each:

- **must-fix M1**: regrade `@objectstack/service-automation` to `minor` in `.changeset/28594-stored-connector-file-ref.md` (keep `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, which is the honest kind and the one PR #28587 used for the same refusal); `Check Changeset` reads the kind once for the PR and refuses `narrowed` with no moved package at `minor`. The PR body's own two lines then stand as written.
- **should-fix S1**: measure a restart with a refused stored row already at rest and report the boot outcome to the seat (detail sent privately).
- **should-fix S2**: file the item-7 finding (by-name, draft and hydration sites still echo a body `_packageId`) as its own card with the shared-helper remedy; link this review.
- **should-fix S3**: correct the Acceptance-notes line in the PR body (only `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is NOT MEASURED).

Nothing built or run. Check-runs on the head at read time: **38 success, 12 skipped, 0 in progress, 0 failed**; `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

**What moved since the record on `43953ed3`** (previous verdict FAIL, must-fix M1, should-fixes S1–S3): M1 is closed (`@objectstack/service-automation` regraded `minor`, kind kept); S1 was measured and turned out real, so this head also makes a stored entry's ref refusal non-fatal at boot, with a reclassification in the classifier, a restart dogfood file, seven reworked and three new unit cases; the docs row and changeset prose say so; S3 (PR body) is corrected. S2 (the item-7 finding) is unchanged and still for the seat to file. The `metadata-protocol` half is byte-identical to the previous head. This is a delta review by the same reviewer on top of the full review; the ① judgments below that the delta does not touch are carried forward as read on `43953ed3` and re-checked against the head's tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Premise.** Holds (measured on base through the real metadata door; the code read agrees).
- **One classifier (item 1).** Still one: `nonHostDeclaringPackageOf` and `createInstalledPackageRefRefusal`. The delta adds no second predicate or message; the per-entry flag (below) wraps the one refusal, it does not reword it.
- **Who reads the host root (item 2).** Unchanged by the delta: only a `code` row or `code` residual whose connector a package registration filed with the same provider binding, or the entry object the host's own artifact reload carried. The only production trigger that passes `metadata.connectors` is the metadata plugin's dev reload of the on-disk artifact; every other trigger passes `{ changed }` only. Registry-stamped, never body-stamped: holds.
- **Stored, authored, environment and stdio rows (item 3).** All refused, now on both roads: saved into a running kernel (the first dogfood file, unchanged) and already at rest when the kernel starts (the new restart file and the new unit restart case). The four reworked unit cases assert the same refusal text, nothing read, the entry absent, and the boot started.
- **Inline and URL controls (item 4).** Unchanged; the restart file re-pins the inline control and the host's own file-ref and stdio entries `ready` after the second boot.
- **Column wins (item 5).** Unchanged (no delta in `metadata-protocol`).
- **Fail-open for doubles (item 6).** Unchanged; the new branch keeps the old reading when the registered layer is absent, and the real registry always offers it.
- **(a) The per-entry flag as the seam.** The right one. The thrown value cannot be matched: the built-in providers wrap the refusal in their own prose, and ADR-0097 invites third-party factories that may wrap it again. The flag is set at the one place the fault is known for certain, inside the refusal closure the materializer itself handed the factory, and it is scoped to the entry whose factory is running (a `let` per loop iteration, read in that iteration's catch). It is wrapped only when the classifier answered `stored`, so an installed or unrecorded entry's refusal never sets it. A factory that dereferences a ref lazily, after it has returned, sets a flag nobody reads, which is harmless. A thrown-value marker (the shape `isConnectorUpstreamUnavailable` uses) would have been the alternative and is defeated by the wrapping; the flag is simpler and cannot be forged by a factory.
